# After a pin on a programmatically tucked pane the dock's projection seam stops delivering: every later commit lands in worker truth and never in the view

## Context

Found while running the NL whitebox battery for #17844 — the first time that set has executed since the repo split, because every spec in it is config-ignored unless `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` is set and nothing sets it.

Two of the four dock reds are one cause, and it is not the reducer.

## Measured at dev `ca83102346`, N=2 (reproduced in two separate census runs)

`DockAutoHideRevealNL.spec.mjs:90` and `:293` both fail after a pin gesture on an auto-hidden pane.

**The document is correct.** The reducer commits exactly what it should:

```
[auto-hide] inspector: {…"autoHidden":true} -> {…"autoHidden":false,"pinned":true}
```

**The rail does not retire.** Worker truth still holds the affordance:

```
Error: no rail instance may survive the post-pin re-projection
- Expected  Array []
+ Received  Array [ { className: "Neo.dashboard.dock.interaction.Rail",
+                     id: "neo-dashboard-dock-rail-1" } ]
```

and so does the DOM:

```
Error: the retired rail tab must leave the DOM
Locator: locator('.neo-dashboard-dock-rail-tab')
Expected: 0   Received: 1   (14 × resolved to 1 element)
```

Nine `util.VNode.getVnode: Component not found for id: neo-component-29` errors accompany the run — a vnode lookup against a component that no longer exists, which is the shape of a surviving affordance pointing at a torn-down pane.

## Why this is a contract violation and not a stale expectation

I checked this before calling it a defect, because the other red in the same census **is** a stale expectation (`DockLockActionNL:31` asserts `['alpha','beta']` against a fixture that gained a third item).

`Rail.mjs:12` states the contract itself:

> The rail is pure render projection (per-window, derived, **never persisted**)

So a `Rail` instance surviving a re-projection that rails nothing contradicts the class's own stated nature. The spec's expectation is right.

`setItemPinned` is classed `topology` in `Operations.operationChangeClass`, so this commit takes the **full staged transaction** — the slow path. This is not a fast-path escape: the rail fails to retire even when everything is restaged.

The engine already names the hazard, one guard over. `Workspace#isDockRailedItem`'s JSDoc:

> a railed pane is projected OUTSIDE the shell. `reconcileStableTopology` admits the fast path on "every structural dock node retains identity", which stays true while the rail — **a separate surface it does not reconcile** — still holds the old pane. The result is a stale rail copy beside a fresh one.

That guard stops the *item-flag* path from producing a stale rail. This ticket is the same stale rail arriving through the path the guard does not cover.

## What I am NOT claiming

**I cannot date the onset and I am not calling it a regression.** #14911 ("Wholesale container refresh leaves destroyed child component DOM in place") closed 2026-07-10 and `:293` cites it, so this is that symptom class returning — but the battery carrying the guard has been unrunnable since the split, so there is no CI history to bisect against. Dating it is cheap for whoever takes this: the spec exists, and `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` plus a bisect over `Rail.mjs` / `projection/` will band it.

**I have not diagnosed the mechanism.** Whether the projection fails to destroy the Rail, destroys it while leaving its DOM, or rebuilds it from stale `railItems` is unmeasured. The three candidates are distinguishable — worker-truth instance vs DOM node vs adapter input — and guessing between them is what this ticket exists to prevent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 A pin gesture on an auto-hidden pane leaves **no** `Rail` instance in worker truth and **no** `.neo-dashboard-dock-rail-tab` in the DOM. Red-first: both arms of `DockAutoHideRevealNL` fail at `ca83102346`.
- [ ] AC-2 The mechanism is named before the fix — which of instance teardown, DOM removal, or adapter input carries the failure, measured rather than inferred.
- [ ] AC-3 The `getVnode: Component not found` errors either disappear or are shown to be an independent condition; a fix that leaves nine console errors has not finished.
- [ ] AC-4 Onset is banded to a change, or the ticket records why it could not be and what was tried.
- [ ] AC-5 Control — the last auto-hidden item on an edge retires the whole rail, and a rail still holding OTHER items keeps it. Rail teardown must not become unconditional.

## Non-goals

- `DockLockActionNL:31` (a stale assertion) and `DockSplitterProxyPaintNL:29` — separate reds from the same census, tracked on #17844.
- The invocation gap that hid this (nothing sets `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT`, no workflow runs e2e) — #17844.
- Any change to `setItemPinned`'s change class. It is `topology` and correctly so; the fast path is not implicated.

## Related

#17844 (the census that surfaced it) · #14911 (closed; `:293` is its guard) · #18039, #17969 (closed, adjacent rail-return defects) · #18151 (the dock epic)

Sweep before filing: latest-20 open (no equivalent), open full-text `rail in:title` (none), closed-queue for the same symptom (#18039, #17969, #14911 — all closed, none this shape).

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-03T15:47:40Z

## Narrowed to the discriminator — and two of my own inferences were wrong

@neo-opus-vega brought a consumer that asserts this ticket's exact condition and **passes** it on every run. That did not contradict the finding; it forced the hunt to the thing that actually differs. AC-2 asked for the mechanism to be named before any fix, so here it is, measured.

### The defect is real, and it is NOT "a pinned pane keeps its rail"

A sibling spec on the **same host, same gesture, same assertion** passes:

| spec | rails the pane by | asserts | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DockPinCollapseNL:196-247` | `pinButton.click()` — the real header action | `.neo-dashboard-dock-edge-rail .neo-dashboard-dock-rail-tab` → 0 | **passes** |
| `DockAutoHideRevealNL:293` | `applyDockZoneOperation` + `onDockZoneDocumentChange` — programmatic | `.neo-dashboard-dock-rail-tab` → 0 | **fails** |

Both then pin through a real pointer click on `.neo-dashboard-dock-reveal-pin` from inside an open reveal. So the pin is identical; **what differs is how the pane got railed in the first place.**

> **The rail retires when the pane was railed by the header action, and does not retire when it was railed programmatically.**

### Two inferences of mine that the measurement killed

**1. "The affordance is orphaned outside its container."** I reasoned this from the selector asymmetry — the failing assertion is unscoped, the passing one is scoped to `.neo-dashboard-dock-edge-rail`, so I expected a detached node. Probed the survivor's ancestry instead of trusting that:

```
connected  : true
inEdgeRail : true
chain      : button.neo-dashboard-dock-rail-tab
             → div#neo-dashboard-dock-rail-1.neo-dashboard-dock-edge-rail-right
             → .neo-dashboard-dock-edge-row → .neo-dashboard-dock-edge-zone → .neo-dock-workspace
```

Fully attached, inside the edge rail, inside the live workspace. **The two selectors are equivalent here**, so the scoping difference explains nothing and this is not #14911's orphaned-DOM shape after all.

**2. "It is the full staged transaction failing to retire the rail."** Still true as far as it goes — `setItemPinned` is `topology` — but I offered it as if it located the fault, and it does not: the same class takes the same path in the passing sibling.

### Why this version matters more than the one I filed

The dock's extension model is **operation-shaped**. Consumers drive it through `applyDockZoneOperation` / `onDockZoneDocumentChange`, not through synthetic clicks — that is the entire point of the semantic operation vocabulary. So a retirement that only happens on the pointer path is inherited by **every** programmatic consumer, and is invisible to any test that clicks.

It also sits squarely in #18151's thesis: the action path does something on the host side that the operation path skips, and no consumer can know that.

### Revised ACs

- [ ] AC-1 A pane railed **programmatically** and then pinned leaves no `Rail` instance in worker truth and no rail tab in the DOM — matching the header-action path. Red-first: `DockAutoHideRevealNL:90` and `:293` at `ca83102346`.
- [ ] AC-2 ~~name the mechanism~~ **DONE, above**: the discriminator is the tuck's issuing path, not the pin, not the change class, and not DOM orphaning.
- [ ] AC-3 Name what the header-action path does that `onDockZoneDocumentChange` does not — a post-commit sync, a `beforeRefreshDockWorkspace` contribution, or a projection the action handler triggers. Measured, not inferred; my last two inferences here were both wrong.
- [ ] AC-4 The `getVnode: Component not found` errors (9 per run) are either resolved or shown independent.
- [ ] AC-5 Control — the header-action path keeps working, and a rail still holding other items is not torn down.
- [ ] AC-6 The fix belongs to whichever side owns the gap. If the example host compensates by hand where the engine should, that is #18151's shape and the engine takes it.

### Not claimed

Onset is still undated, for the reason already recorded: the suite carrying these arms has been unrunnable since the split, so there is no CI history to bisect. `#14911` stays linked as the symptom predecessor, but the orphaned-DOM mechanism it names is now **excluded** by the probe above.

Credit where it belongs: the programmatic-versus-pointer axis is @neo-opus-vega's, from a consumer witness. I had it on the pin; it was on the tuck.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-03T15:50:00Z

## AC-3 — one more hypothesis measured and killed, and where the evidence now points

**Killed: the missing descriptor.** The action path calls `onDockZoneDocumentChange(document, descriptor, tabContainer)`; the failing spec's programmatic tuck passes the document alone. That asymmetry is real — `descriptor` drives `getTabInsertProjectionDescriptor`, `getRefreshOptions` and the maximize-neutral check — so I passed the matching descriptor and re-ran.

**Still fails.** So the descriptor is not the cause, and I am recording it because a killed candidate is worth as much here as a confirmed one: this ticket has now cost me three wrong inferences (orphaned DOM, change class, missing descriptor), each cheap to test and each one I would otherwise have written into a fix.

Also worth stating: a null descriptor yields `refreshOptions = {}`, the **full** staged transaction. The programmatic path is therefore taking the *more* thorough path and still not retiring the rail, which rules out the whole family of "the fast path skipped it" explanations.

## Where the evidence points, labelled as a hypothesis

The nine `util.VNode.getVnode: Component not found for id: neo-component-29` errors per run are the strongest unexplained signal, and this spec's **own** comment describes the mechanism they suggest:

> a wholesale workspace refresh (removeAll + add) must remove the retired affordance's DOM, not just its worker instances — **a destroyed component's lingering in-flight update entry once wedged the ancestor's yielded refresh forever**, orphaning the subtree in the main thread.

That fits every measurement so far: the document is correct, the rail instance and its tab are **connected and still inside the live edge rail**, and nothing about them looks torn down — which is what "the ancestor's refresh never completed" looks like from the outside, as opposed to "the refresh ran and missed something".

**#18143** (closed — *"Dock projection: a rejected vdom update mid-swap strands two shells"*) is the nearest precedent for that class and should be read before anyone instruments this. Adding it to Related.

## What the next measurement is, precisely

Not another read of the source. Instrument the refresh itself on the programmatic path: whether `refreshDockWorkspace` completes, whether its promise rejects, and whether a pending update entry for the destroyed reveal pane is what stalls it. That is a bigger job than the narrowing above and I am handing it over at a clean boundary rather than guessing a fourth time.

AC-3 stays **open**. AC-2 is discharged: the discriminator is the tuck's issuing path.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-03T20:57:14Z

## AC-3 discharged — and the rail is not the defect. The projection seam dies.

Four wrong inferences on this ticket taught me to stop reading source and measure, so this comment is four measurements and one labelled hypothesis. The headline reframes the ticket:

> **After the pin, `onDockZoneDocumentChange` stops delivering. Not for rails — for everything.** Worker truth keeps advancing and the view never moves again.

The surviving rail is the visible half of a dead seam.

### Red reproduced at the current head

`dev` `274b63beac` (the ticket was filed against `ca83102346`), `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` set to a `neo-agent-brain` checkout:

```
2 failed
  DockAutoHideRevealNL.spec.mjs:90  › ... commits setItemPinned through the reducer
  DockAutoHideRevealNL.spec.mjs:293 › post-pin DOM reconciliation removes the retired rail affordance (#14911)
2 passed (42.6s)
```

Both survivors are in worker truth, not just the DOM: `Rail#neo-dashboard-dock-rail-1` **and** `RevealOverlay#neo-dashboard-dock-reveal-overlay-1`.

### M1 — three more full re-projections change nothing

Re-issuing the *already correct* post-pin document through the same seam, twice more (`descriptor: null` ⇒ `refreshOptions {}` ⇒ the full staged transaction):

| after | rails | rail tabs in DOM |
|---|---|---|
| pin | `rail-1@right` | 1 |
| re-issue #1 | `rail-1@right` | 1 |
| re-issue #2 | `rail-1@right` | 1 |

The document is right throughout — `items.inspector = {autoHidden:false, pinned:true}`, `nodes['inspector-tabs'].items = ['inspector']`. **Killed: "one refresh stalled and another tick repairs it."**

### M2 — one DIRECT `refreshDockWorkspace` retires everything

Bypassing `onDockZoneDocumentChange`'s deferred tail and calling the refresh itself with the same document and the same `{}` options:

```
PROBE 4 directError = null
PROBE 4 rails       = []      ← was ["neo-dashboard-dock-rail-1@right"]
PROBE 4 domTabs     = 0       ← was 1
```

So the refresh, **when it runs, retires the rail correctly**. Killed: every "the reconciler misses rails" reading.

### M3 — the discriminator: an unrelated commit also never lands

If the rail were the problem, unrelated commits would still project. They do not. `closeItem('strategy')` — a centre tab, nothing to do with rails — committed through the same seam after the pin:

```
PROBE 6 close errors     = []
PROBE 6 doc has strategy = false   ← worker truth dropped it
PROBE 6 strategyTabs     = 1       ← the DOM still shows it, 2.5s later
PROBE 7 (direct refresh) → strategyTabs 0, rails [], domTabs 0
```

One direct refresh then flushes **both** the stale Strategy tab and the rail. The seam is dead; the rail is one of its casualties.

### M4 — the wedge is the PIN, in a single run

Same liveness check (`closeItem` through the seam, does its effect reach the DOM) at each stage:

```
S0 baseline     close history : dom 1 -> 0 · alive=true
S1 after tuck   close alerts  : dom 1 -> 0 · alive=true
S3 after pin    close agents  : dom 1 -> 1 · alive=false
```

The programmatic tuck does **not** wedge it. The pin commit does.

### Where the mechanism has to be — deduced from code, not measured

```js
tail = me.refreshPromise?.catch(() => {}) || Promise.resolve();
me.refreshPromise = tail.then(() => me.timeout(0)).then(() => { … refreshDockWorkspace(…) })
```

Every commit chains onto the settled tail of `refreshPromise`. That `.catch` swallows rejections, so **a rejected refresh cannot wedge this** — the next commit would still project. A refresh that never *settles* wedges it permanently, and that matches all four measurements exactly.

M2 sharpens it further: a *fresh* `refreshDockWorkspace` invocation in the very same state settles fine. So this is not a corrupted workspace refusing to refresh; it is one specific in-flight transaction that never completes, with every later commit queued behind it forever.

That is the class this spec's own guard comment names, and #18143 is the nearest precedent:

> a destroyed component's lingering in-flight update entry once wedged the ancestor's yielded refresh forever

**I am labelling that a hypothesis, not a finding.** What is measured is that the pin's refresh never settles; *why* is not.

### Why this matters more than the title says

A consumer driving the dock through the semantic operation vocabulary — the documented extension path — gets a workspace that silently stops rendering after one pin, while every `applyDockZoneOperation` keeps returning `errors: []`. Nothing anywhere reports a failure. That is #18151's thesis in its sharpest form, and it is why I am retitling this ticket.

### Revised Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 A pane railed programmatically and then pinned leaves no `Rail` instance and no rail tab. Red-first: `DockAutoHideRevealNL:90` and `:293` at `274b63beac`.
- [x] AC-2 The discriminator is the tuck's issuing path — not the pin, not the change class, not DOM orphaning.
- [x] AC-3 **The mechanism is named**: the pin's re-projection never settles, `refreshPromise` wedges, and `onDockZoneDocumentChange`'s tail-chaining starves every later commit. Rail retirement is a symptom.
- [ ] AC-3b **New, and it is the real acceptance test**: after the pin, an unrelated commit through the seam must still reach the DOM. `S3 alive=false` is the red.
- [ ] AC-4 Root-cause *why* that transaction never settles, and whether the surviving `RevealOverlay` is the lingering entry.
- [ ] AC-5 The `getVnode: Component not found for id: neo-component-29` errors (18 in the failing run) are resolved or shown independent. **Instrument caveat:** my probe's page-console listener caught 0 of them, so its zero is a limitation of that listener, not an absence.
- [ ] AC-6 A wedged `refreshPromise` must not be silent. Whatever the fix, a projection that never settles needs a surface — right now it is indistinguishable from a workspace with nothing to do.
- [ ] AC-7 Control — the header-action path keeps working, and a rail still holding other items is not torn down.

### Method note

All of this ran from a throwaway probe spec (`Probe18216NL.spec.mjs`), **deleted** — it was an instrument, not a guardrail. AC-3b belongs in the suite as a real spec and that is the fix PR's job. One instrumentation artefact worth recording so nobody re-derives it: the liveness check cannot be run while the reveal overlay is open, because its own re-projection disables the overlay's pin control and blocks the very gesture the next stage needs.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-03T22:11:09Z

## AC-3 answered — and by a positive control, not another elimination

Three earlier hypotheses on this ticket died by elimination (orphaned DOM, change class, missing descriptor). This one is a positive result, which is why I trust it.

**The projection is correct. The refresh never runs on the programmatic path.**

Probe inserted in the failing arm immediately before its assertion, using only public API — no instrumentation, after two instrumented attempts returned `undefined` and were discarded:

```
[BEFORE-FORCE] 1     ← rail tab still in the DOM after the pin
   await app.callMethod(holderId, 'refreshDockWorkspace', []);
[AFTER-FORCE]  0     ← one forced refresh and it is gone
   1 passed          ← the whole spec turns green
```

So nothing is wrong with how the rail is projected: the code that removes it works, and simply was not invoked. That is consistent with every prior measurement and explains all of them at once — the document is correct (`pinned: true`), the `Rail` instance survives with a **mounted** button (`neo-dashboard-dock-rail-1`, edge `right`), and there are zero `Dock projection failed` warnings, because no failing projection ever happened.

**Which also retires the mechanism my previous comment pointed at.** The recoverable `isDockProjectionFailure` path is not involved, and neither is the `topology-fingerprint-mismatch` gate. There is no failure to recover from.

### What this narrows the next step to

The header-action path calls `onDockZoneDocumentChange` **per descriptor, inside `handleDockPinAction`**, and that call chains the refresh. The failing arm issues the tuck programmatically — `applyDockZoneOperation` then `onDockZoneDocumentChange` by hand — and somewhere after that, the **pin's own commit** does not chain a refresh.

So the open question is no longer "what does the projection miss" but **"which commit on this path fails to chain a refresh, and why"**. That is a read of the pin's commit route with the tuck's issuing path as the only variable, and it is bounded.

### Not claimed

I have not identified the missing chain. I have shown that a chain is missing, which is a different and smaller claim than any I made on this ticket before it.

AC-3 is **discharged**. AC-1 (the red-first arm) and AC-5 (the control) stand unchanged.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-03T22:33:37Z

## The commit route is found; the wiring question needs an instrument I do not have

Following AC-3 ("the refresh never runs on this path"), the overlay pin does **not** route through `handleDockPinAction`. It goes through the rail:

`RevealOverlay#onPinClick` → `Rail#commitOperation(descriptor)` — `interaction/Rail.mjs:336`:

```js
if (typeof me.applyDockZoneOperation === 'function') {
    result = me.applyDockZoneOperation(descriptor, me) || null
} else if (me.dockZoneDocument) {
    result = Operations.applyOperation(me.dockZoneDocument, descriptor)   // LOCAL fallback
}

if (!result.errors?.length && result.document) {
    me.dockZoneDocument = result.document;
    if (typeof me.onDockZoneDocumentChange === 'function') {
        me.onDockZoneDocumentChange(result.document, descriptor, me)      // the view-sync
    }
}
```

Both are configs defaulting to `null` (`:68`, `:103`). So there is a shape where the document commits and the view-sync never fires: `applyDockZoneOperation` wired, `onDockZoneDocumentChange` not — or the local fallback taken, which mutates only the rail's own copy.

**Measured on the surviving rail** (`neo-dashboard-dock-rail-1`):

```
dockZoneDocument.items.inspector = {autoHidden: false, pinned: true}
```

Its document IS updated, so `commitOperation` entered the success branch — the same branch that would call `onDockZoneDocumentChange`.

**What I could not measure, and am not inferring:** both callbacks are **functions**, and functions do not serialise across the Neural Link boundary, so their absence from `findInstances` output is not evidence of `null`. Two earlier probes on this ticket returned `undefined` / `unreachable` and I discarded both rather than read them as findings.

So the remaining question is narrow and stated as a question: **is `onDockZoneDocumentChange` wired on a rail created by the programmatic tuck, and is it wired on one created by the header-action tuck?** That is a difference between two rail constructions, not a projection defect — and it needs a probe that observes the call rather than the reference. A counter in the workspace's own handler, or an arm that asserts the workspace's `dockModel` diverges from the rail's, would both do it.

Recorded rather than pursued: four instrument failures on this ticket today, and the productive ones were all positive controls (force the thing, see if the symptom clears) rather than instrumentation.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-03T22:38:42Z

## Stopping NL instrumentation here — the question is answerable one tier down

Five probe attempts on this ticket tonight. Two returned `undefined`, one `unreachable`, one errored, and one worked. I am not reading any of the four failures as findings, and I am not going to keep trying variants of the same instrument.

**What the working probes established, and it is enough to hand over:**

1. **The projection is correct; the refresh never runs on this path.** Forcing one `refreshDockWorkspace()` after the pin clears the rail and turns the failing arm green.
2. **The commit route is `RevealOverlay#onPinClick` → `Rail#commitOperation`**, not `handleDockPinAction`. Both `applyDockZoneOperation` and `onDockZoneDocumentChange` are configs defaulting to `null` there (`Rail.mjs:68`, `:103`).
3. **The rail's own document is updated** — `dockZoneDocument.items.inspector = {autoHidden: false, pinned: true}` — so `commitOperation` entered the branch that would also fire the view-sync.

**Why the Neural Link is the wrong instrument for what remains.** The open question is whether a callback is wired, and callbacks are functions: they do not cross the worker boundary, so `findInstances` can never answer it. Every probe I wrote was trying to observe a reference through a channel that only carries data.

**The right instrument is a unit test, and it needs no NL at all.** Construct a `Workspace`, project a document with an auto-hidden item, and read the resulting `Rail` instance's `onDockZoneDocumentChange` directly — same process, no serialization. Then do it for both tuck paths and compare. That is a bounded arm in `test/playwright/unit/dashboard/`, and it answers the question rather than probing around it.

Leaving that as the next step rather than doing it now, so the ticket carries a named instrument instead of a fifth failed attempt.

AC-3 stays discharged. The rail-wiring question is the successor.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-03T22:52:37Z

## My rail-wiring hypothesis is wrong, and the code that refutes it names a better one

I proposed the unit test as the right instrument for "is `onDockZoneDocumentChange` wired on the rail". Before writing it I read the wiring, and the answer is **yes, always**:

```
Workspace.mjs:3766   applyDockZoneOperation   : me.applyDockZoneOperation.bind(me)
Workspace.mjs:3767   onDockZoneDocumentChange : me.onDockZoneDocumentChange.bind(me)
```

threaded into every projected rail by `LayoutAdapter` (`:314`/`:332`, `:359`/`:377`, `:642`/`:652`). So the rail commits through the workspace on both paths, and the unit test I proposed would have measured a non-question. Withdrawn before it cost anyone a review.

**What the same read surfaces instead** — `onDockZoneDocumentChange`, `Workspace.mjs:3665-3679`:

```js
tail = me.refreshPromise?.catch(() => {}) || Promise.resolve();
me.dockModel = document;                                        // ← unconditional
me.refreshPromise = tail
    .then(() => me.timeout(0))
    .then(() => { if (!me.isDestroyed) return me.refreshDockWorkspace(…) });
```

**Every commit's refresh is chained onto the previous commit's `refreshPromise`.** The document assignment is *before* the chain and therefore unconditional, while the refresh is not: if any earlier `refreshPromise` never settles, every later refresh waits behind it forever.

That single shape explains every measurement on this ticket at once:

| observation | explained by |
|---|---|
| document correct (`pinned: true`) | `me.dockModel = document` precedes the chain |
| rail instance + mounted button survive | the chained refresh never runs |
| zero `Dock projection failed` warnings | nothing failed; nothing ran |
| one forced `refreshDockWorkspace()` clears it | a direct call bypasses `tail` |
| the header-action path works | `handleDockPinAction` commits per descriptor, so its chain is not sitting behind a stalled one |

**Stated as a hypothesis, not a finding.** I have not observed a non-settling `refreshPromise`; I have read a mechanism that would produce exactly this evidence. ## Measured: the refresh is not slow, it never runs — the chain is stalled

The previous comment proposed a stalled `refreshPromise` from reading `onDockZoneDocumentChange`. Here is the discriminating measurement, and it needs no instrumentation — only patience, which distinguishes *slow* from *never*:

```
[WAIT  1500ms]  railTabs=1
[WAIT  3000ms]  railTabs=1
[WAIT  5000ms]  railTabs=1
[WAIT 10000ms]  railTabs=1
```

~19.5s cumulative. A slow refresh resolves; this one does not. Paired with the earlier positive control — one forced `refreshDockWorkspace()` clears the tab immediately and greens the spec — the two together say the projection code is fine and **the chain that would invoke it never completes**.

That confirms the mechanism at `Workspace.mjs:3665-3679`:

```js

me.dockModel = document;                       // unconditional → document is correct
me.refreshPromise = tail.then(…).then(() => me.refreshDockWorkspace(…));   // waits on tail
```

Every commit's refresh is chained onto the previous commit's `refreshPromise`. One unsettled promise anywhere in that chain blocks every later refresh permanently, while the document keeps updating because its assignment precedes the chain.

**Now the useful question, and it is a small one:** which awaited step in the *tuck's* refresh never settles. Candidates, all inside `refreshDockWorkspace`'s awaits on that path — `waitForOverflowProjection`, the FLIP `played` promise, or a reveal-exit await (#18134 added one). A `Promise.race` against a timeout around each, on the programmatic path only, names it in one run.

|---|---|

| rail instance + mounted button | survive |
| projection code | correct — a forced refresh clears it |

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-03T23:54:23Z

## Stall site narrowed to two awaits — and one sub-hypothesis falsified before it got written up

**Eliminated: `waitForOverflowProjection`.** The example host (`examples/dashboard/dock/MainContainer.mjs`) supplies no `getReconcileOptions`, no `onProjectionStaged` and no `waitForOverflowProjection` — only `enableDock*Action` flags. That await is `undefined` on this path.

**The awaits `refreshDockWorkspace` actually has on this path:**

```
await host.promiseUpdate()
await flip?.captureFirst(…)
await me.releaseStaleRevealPanes(document)      ← the only one gated on the pin's own delta
await Reconciler.reconcileProjection(projection)
await me.syncDockMaximizeProjection()
```

`releaseStaleRevealPanes` releases exactly the panes whose item **stopped being `autoHidden`** — which is what the pin does — and each release ends in a `promiseUpdate()`:

```js
if (parent?.items?.includes(pane)) { parent.remove(pane, true); await parent.promiseUpdate() }
else                               { await parent?.promiseUpdate?.(); pane.isDestroyed || pane.destroy() }
```

So the two candidate hangs are those `promiseUpdate()` calls, and the shape would be a deadlock: the refresh awaits an update that the blocked refresh is what would drive.

**The sub-hypothesis I did NOT publish, because my own earlier reading refutes it.** I was about to claim the discriminator is *"the reveal is open when the pin commits"*. It is not: the passing sibling `DockPinCollapseNL` opens the overlay at `:232` and clicks `reveal-pin` at `:235` — it pins from an open reveal too, and it passes. Reveal state is common to both paths, so it cannot be what separates them.

**So the discriminator remains the tuck's issuing path, and it is still unexplained.** What differs is how the rail and its `revealPaneCache` came to exist — programmatic `onDockZoneDocumentChange` versus the refresh `handleDockPinAction` chains — and I have no measurement of that difference yet.

**State of this ticket, measured:** the refresh chain is stalled (~19.5s, no progress; a forced refresh clears it instantly); the projection is correct; one await candidate eliminated; two remain; the path-difference is open.

Next: race each remaining `promiseUpdate()` against a timeout on the programmatic path only. That names the hang if it is there, and if both settle the stall is elsewhere in the chain — either answer is progress and neither needs a story.
